transcript.text: Just got a new Siemens dishwasher and there's always a bit of water left in the bottom under the filter after it finishes. Is it draining properly?

Yes — if it is only a small amount of clean water sitting in the sump underneath the filter, and it is below the filter level, that is normally correct. Dishwashers retain a little water there to keep the pump and seals from drying out. It would suggest a drainage problem only if the water is dirty or smells, rises above the filter/base, or the machine leaves water visible across the bottom of the tub after a programme. 1. With the dishwasher switched off, lift out the filter and look at the water level and condition. A small, clean amount only in the well underneath is normal.
2. If there is more than that, rinse the filter and clear any food debris from the sump beneath it. A partial blockage is the common simple cause.
3. If it is newly installed and has standing water after cycles, check the drain hose is not kinked and that the connection under the sink drains freely; an installation restriction can prevent proper draining. Is the water only a small, clean amount below the filter level, or is it dirty/smelly or sitting above the filter?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]

Thanks. I checked: it's a small amount of clean water, roughly a cupful, just in the well under the filter. None in the main tub. The filter itself is clean and the water level is the same the next day, not rising. Is that normal then?

Yes — that is normal. A cupful of clean water held in the sump well beneath the filter, with no water in the main tub and no rise overnight, is the normal residual water that keeps the pump and seals from drying out. It is draining properly based on those signs. No action is needed. Only investigate if water starts appearing across the tub base, rises above the filter, becomes dirty or smelly, or the dishwasher reports a drain fault.
